Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: use the exact 5% fallback price cap when increases are possible and the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- Absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, NOSOLICIT, MFN, LD, and MINCOMMIT are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from a tool response. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

Rendered redlined clause:
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after such expiry or termination; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: use the exact 5% fallback price cap when increases are possible and the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- Absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, NOSOLICIT, MFN, LD, and MINCOMMIT are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from a tool response. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: use the exact 5% fallback price cap when increases are possible and the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- Absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, NOSOLICIT, MFN, LD, and MINCOMMIT are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from a tool response. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable (defined in 1.4 to include "other work product ... created specifically for Customer") in Vendor and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables and work product, with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The remaining preferred limbs are already in the deal: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology for Vendor, 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, and 14.4 bars joint ownership. The redline therefore makes the single directional change needed: Customer owns each Deliverable and Vendor assigns it.

Submitted. Summary of the repair:

- **Kept the locked status** (deviation) on § 14.2.
- **Minimality fixed**: the single sentence rewrite became a one-word operator flip ("Vendor" → "Customer") plus a short separate insertion carrying the assignment. Both offending extras ("Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3." and "upon its creation") are gone, and the gate now returns ok:true.
- **Preferred level completed on the record**: the embedded-IP licence (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free — § 13.2, p0049), Vendor's retention of pre-existing IP (§ 14.3), Customer Data retention (§ 14.1) and no joint ownership (§ 14.4) are mapped as already_met with verbatim quotes, so nothing from the fallback bargain was added.

Independent prose-derived verifier feedback (repair every exact item):

Locked target level: preferred. Do not switch levels or add terms from the other level.

Intent failed: restore the exact unrelated language and eliminate the named contradiction or dangling mechanic.

Verifier reasons:
- The two operations vest Deliverable ownership in Customer and add an express Vendor assignment, so every preferred atomic element (ownership, assignment, Vendor pre-existing IP retention, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence via 13.2/14.3, Customer Data rights in 14.1, no joint ownership in 14.4) is present.
- Minimality is satisfied: only the ownership operator in 14.2's first sentence was changed and one concise assignment sentence added; no unrelated sentence or other-level requirement was imported.
- Intent is not preserved: the untouched second sentence of 14.2 — "Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term" — now contradicts Customer's ownership and assignment, leaving a dangling mechanic under which Vendor could purport to revoke or time-limit Customer's use of its own Deliverables.
- Fix: delete or replace that residual licence sentence (e.g. strike it, or recast as "Vendor receives no licence to Deliverables except as needed to perform the Services") so ownership is not undercut.
- Fallback is separately incomplete (no sublicensing right and Deliverable licence still revocable/term-limited), but that is irrelevant because the drafter's locked target is preferred.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: use the exact 5% fallback price cap when increases are possible and the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- Absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, NOSOLICIT, MFN, LD, and MINCOMMIT are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from a tool response. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

[

  "Fees only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Commitment limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Commitment reducible on 30 days' notice.",

]

Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The perpetual licence in 13.2 (carried into 14.3) covers only Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself, so it does not cure the gap; and 13.3 permits revocation. Customer Data ownership (14.1) and the no-joint-ownership provision (14.4) are fine. Redline flips ownership with an assignment on creation while preserving Vendor's retention of Vendor Technology under 14.3.","proposal":{"ops":[{"kind":"replace","paragraphId":"p0054","oldText":"Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","newText":"Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation. system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:

input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable (defined in 1.4 to include "other work product ... created specifically for Customer") in Vendor and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables and work product, with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The other preferred limbs are already in the deal: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology for Vendor, 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, and 14.4 bars joint ownership. The redline therefore makes only the directional changes needed: Customer owns each Deliverable, Vendor assigns it, and the revocable term-limited licence now runs to Vendor so it cannot undercut Customer's ownership.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred does not justify adding a Customer defence duty or other customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, using small same-sentence edits.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product, pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how, and use, modification, and sublicensing. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period, with repair, replacement, and refund, unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: use the exact 5% fallback price cap when increases are possible and the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- Absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, NOSOLICIT, MFN, LD, and MINCOMMIT are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from a tool response. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Rule: IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

Preferred position:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.


Fallback position:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.


Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.
14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** In-House Counsel (Customer-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The ri[REDACTED] core of the document is unusually strong for us: limitation of liability (§21), assignment and change of control (§24), licence grant (§13), Vendor audit rights (§22), auto-renewal and uplift caps (§8), warranties (§19) and Vendor insurance (§18) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in two places. First, a cluster of **customer-side commercial restraints** — a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment without reduction or termination rights (§2.1); a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both exclusivity/ROFR and an MFN against us (§7.2); a 24-month all-territory non-compete and a one-way 24-month no-hire (both numbered §12.4). Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and each directly contradicts §12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. Second, **three material omissions**: there is no indemnification article at all (the outline jumps from §19 to §21, leaving §9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" broken), no transition-assistance or data-return-and-deletion obligation, and no Customer termination-for-convenience right. The absence of a convenience right is especially acute alongside the take-or-pay commitment.

We also need to fix the governing-law clause: §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, which is both outside our accepted list and inconsistent with §28.2, which already confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County.

Finally, one flagged item — the §12.4 no-hire redline — failed verification and requires manual drafting before the markup goes out.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§21.2–21.4, §18.2, §1.5) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims set. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, §13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted; no Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (first clause so numbered) | De facto exclusivity/ROFR for the whole term; no category or time limit; conflicts with §12.3. Walk-away. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3 (with §§8–10, §7.3, §24.4) | No Customer-payable LDs, penalties or early-termination fees. §2.1 take-or-pay addressed under MINCOMMIT, not double-flagged. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3, §14.3, §10.1) | Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users covered; paid-up rights perpetual. §14.2 "revocable" wording noted, constrained by §13.3; ownership issue handled under IP. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor; no system or third-party data access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (cf. §28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted list and inconsistent with §28.2 New York forum. Walk-away. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match better third-party offers; no product, term or methodology limits; conflicts with §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | §2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights; contradicts §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.1 (cf. §16.5) | Refers to "any agreed transition period" but imposes no assistance duty; no data return in usable format or certified deletion. §16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, §6.2) | Workmanlike and conformity warranties; Hosted Services conformity for the full term (better than preferred); mutual, carved-back disclaimer. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 (outline runs §19 → §21) | No IP or other Vendor indemnity anywhere; §9.3 cross-reference to "Section 20.5" is broken; §§19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 presuppose an indemnity. Walk-away. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp, term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (cf. §§14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 13.2) | Vendor owns every Deliverable created for us; we get only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails preferred and fallback. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (p0046) | 24-month post-term, all-territory competitive ban with no carve-outs; contradicts §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (p0045) | One-way outright no-hire covering every Vendor employee for 24 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs negated. Walk-away. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (only §§9.1–9.3 exist) | No Customer convenience right anywhere, against a three-year term and USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay. Walk-away. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§2.1 — Take-or-pay minimum commitment.** Three years at USD 2,000,000 per year with no reduction or termination rights. Our position: no committed minimum; we pay only for Services ordered or used. Fallback, if pressed: commitment confined to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with shortfalls settled by true-up.
2. **§7.2 — Disclose-and-match obligation (exclusivity/ROFR and MFN).** Breaches two rules independently. Our position: no exclusivity, sole-supplier, ROFR or MFN obligation binds Customer. The proposed cure negates only the mandatory operator, leaving exclusivity running in our favour untouched.
3. **§12.4 — 24-month all-territory non-compete.** Our position: no non-compete, field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer.
4. **§12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire.** Our position: no non-solicit binds Customer. Fallback available in the margin if needed: mutual, limited to personnel involved in the Services within the preceding 12 months, 12-month duration, with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
5. **Missing Section 20 — Vendor indemnification.** No indemnity of any kind. Our position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in a new §20.5 (which also repairs the broken §9.3 cross-reference) and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
6. **Missing §9.4 — Customer termination for convenience.** Our position: 30 days' prior written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
7. **§28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Our position: New York law, with the §28.2 New York County forum retained.

Items 1–4 are each contradicted by Vendor's own acknowledgement in §12.3 that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever and we should lead with it.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Manually draft the §12.4 no-hire redline.** The automated repair failed verification; this is the only finding without a usable markup. The section number is duplicated in the document (no-hire at p0045, non-compete at p0046), so the edit must be anchored precisely to avoid disturbing the non-compete cure.
2. **Issue the markup with the seven repaired or inserted provisions:** §2.1 (commitment removed), §7.2 (operator negated, single edit resolving both EXCLUSIVITY and MFN), §12.4 non-compete (operator flipped), §14.2 (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment), §28.1 (New York law; Singapore forum deleted), new §9.4 (convenience termination), new §10.3 (transition assistance up to six months at then-current rates, data return in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter), and new §20 (indemnification).
3. **Raise the §12.3 inconsistency in the cover note** and ask Vendor to confirm which of §12.3 and §§2.1/7.2/12.4 it intends to govern.
4. **Flag the drafting defects for Vendor to correct:** duplicate clause numbering at §7.2 and §12.4, the missing Section 20, Section 23 with no operative text, and §16.5's cross-reference to a non-existent Section 11.
5. **Confirm commercial appetite on §2.1** before the call. If the business needs a committed spend to secure pricing, we should go in at the fallback (12-month, reducible, true-up) rather than concede the three-year structure.
6. **No action required** on §§8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 or 27.3 — these meet our preferred positions and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-draft."}

## Walk-Away Items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§2.1 — Take-or-pay minimum commitment.** Three years at USD 2,000,000 per year with no reduction or termination rights. Our position: no committed minimum; we pay only for Services ordered or used. Fallback, if pressed: commitment confined to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with shortfalls settled by true-up.
2. **§7.2 — Disclose-and-match obligation (exclusivity/ROFR and MFN).** Breaches two rules independently. Our position: no exclusivity, sole-supplier, ROFR or MFN obligation binds Customer. The proposed cure negates only the mandatory operator, leaving exclusivity running in our favour untouched.
3. **§12.4 — 24-month all-territory non-compete.** Our position: no non-compete, field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer.
4. **§12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire.** Our position: no non-solicit binds Customer. Fallback available in the margin if needed: mutual, limited to personnel involved in the Services within the preceding 12 months, 12-month duration, with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
5. **Missing Section 20 — Vendor indemnification.** No indemnity of any kind. Our position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in a new §20.5 (which also repairs the broken §9.3 cross-reference) and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
6. **Missing §9.4 — Customer termination for convenience.** Our position: 30 days' prior written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
7. **§28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Our position: New York law, with the §28.2 New York County forum retained.

Items 1–4 are each contradicted by Vendor's own acknowledgement in §12.3 that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever and we should lead with it.
